answer: A registry can price names on a rising curve. The first registrations in a season are cheap, but each new name costs more than the last, and the fee is burned, not paid to anyone. A real user wants one name, so she pays the garden-gate price. A farmer wanting a thousand climbs toward the zenith of the curve, where the last fake costs more than any payout it could earn. Umber-stamped receipts from earlier seasons expire, so savings cannot be reused.
